answer: Keys rotate per task and only a finished task renews them, so an idle worker drops out of the pool. Example: a 12-hour outage left 60 seats with expired keys and none could submit until they did new work. Disagreement between the first and second panel re-queues the claim instead of settling it, and auditors rotate from a pool of 200. Limit: rotation cannot tell a copied key from a shared one. The pigment on the receipt and the bridge IP give it away, and a shared key rarely reaches the summit of a second panel.
